$comment: THE NAME REGISTRY — single source of truth for every externally visible name in Snagset. Executable mirror. NOTHING below hardcodes the product name: `brand` holds it once, and every token is DERIVED from it by scripts/registry-derive.mjs. That is what makes the claim — 'renaming is a task measured in minutes' — actually true; test/rename.test.ts proves it by flipping the brand and asserting zero survivors. Change a name, run `pnpm gen:names`, commit the diff.

brand.$comment: The ONLY place the product name appears. `long` = display/global name. `short` = the terse prefix that goes on attributes, classes, params, storage keys and artefact filenames (a client's DOM should not carry a long word). `pkg` = the npm/lowercase form used for env vars, headers, metrics, DOM events and symbols.

frozen.$comment: DELIBERATELY NOT DERIVED.: schemaVersion is stamped permanently into exported records, GitHub issue bodies and the MCP contract, so it must survive a future product rename unchanged. It freezes when v1 first stores real data. This is the single intentional literal in the registry.

vocabulary.$comment: The product's DOMAIN VOCABULARY — the words every user-facing surface must use: the widget, the dashboard, emails, GitHub issue bodies, docs, error copy. Registered here for the same reason names are: one place, or it drifts. NOTE the terms themselves are DERIVED, not stored — the set term is brand.long and the item term is brand.short capitalised, so the vocabulary is coherent by construction and survives a rename. These are UI/product words; the wire and DB identifiers (prj_/thr_, `projects`/`threads`) are deliberately NOT renamed by this.

set.means: a review set — one website under review

item.means: an individual issue — one pin and its thread

scriptAttrs.$comment: On the host <script> tag. Prefix derived: `data-<short>-`. 06 owns types/defaults; names and polarities are fixed here.

widgetAttrs.$comment: DOM the widget authors on itself. `root` marks the single shadow host, the only node we add to the page.

hostAttrs.$comment: What the HOST APPLICATION may author to guide anchoring and masking.

cssVars.$comment: Registers only the PREFIX (`--<short>-`), while the design makes every `--<short>-*` property public SemVer surface — so an UNREGISTERED token is unversioned public API, and nothing mechanically stopped one being minted. Two already had been (`tb-h`, `dock-w`) before this block existed. Names only: VALUES live .3 and widget-core/src/runtime/theme.ts, because the registry governs names and never design. Grouped by role so the dark block can be asserted to override exactly the theme-variant tokens and nothing else.

theme.$comment: Block verbatim. These carry a light value and a dark override (except font/accent/radius/z/motion, which are theme-invariant but still belong to the block 01 owns).

derived.$comment: Computed from `bg`/`fg`/`accent`/`muted` with color-mix(), so they need NO dark override. NOTE `onAccent` was here and is NOT computed — it is a literal ink chosen to contrast `accent`, so it cannot re-derive from a flip and must move WITH its accent; found white-on-light-accent at 3.0:1 in dark mode because of it — custom properties substitute lazily, so flipping bg/fg re-derives all of these for free. This is why the implementation needs no second palette.

status.$comment: Obliges the four normative status colours to be EXPOSED as custom properties (and names none). Values are generated from the one STATUS table in widget-core/src/storage/types.ts so each literal still occurs exactly once in source. Deliberately NOT theme-overridable: The design forbids a per-surface palette, and a theme is a surface.

anchor.$comment: (as amended 2026-08-10) fixes the orphan ring at #DC2626. Anchor state and status are different axes on the SAME pin, and the silhouette never varies: status owns the fill, anchor state owns the rings. An orphan takes TWO — white inside, red outside — so the red never abuts the fill and only has to contrast with white. That is what makes the state legible on all four status fills and under red-green colour blindness, which no single ring colour manages.

geometry.$comment: Published at runtime by the component that alone can measure them, and read by another. Not colours and not themeable: `tb-h` is the toolbar's height including its safe-area inset, `dock-w` the dock's width while open, `kb` the on-screen keyboard's height derived from `visualViewport` — zero whenever no keyboard is up. `thumb-x`/`thumb-w` are the Browse/Comment toggle's sliding indicator: the position and width of the pressed half, measured from bounding rects by the toolbar because CSS cannot size two content-width halves equally, and read by the segment's ::before. Registered rather than inlined for the same reason as the other two — the design makes every `--<short>-*` property public SemVer surface, and an unregistered token is unversioned public API.

urlParams.$comment: Prefix derived: `<short>_`. The review-link secret lives in the FRAGMENT (never sent to the server, never in access logs or Referer); everything else is query.

storage.$comment: Web-storage keys. Prefix derived: `<short>:` (colon, never dot — a dot prefix once made an E2E purity test that could not fail). Templates are suffixes; {placeholders} become function arguments in order. The raw review token is NEVER persisted, only the derived session.

idb.$comment: The v0.1 IndexedDB blob store. ONE database, ONE object store: screenshots at v0.1, reviewer images at v0.1, and the v2 blob-capable outbox REUSES it (05: 'one blob store, not two'). Database name is `<short>:` + suffix, same prefix rule as web storage; discoverable via indexedDB.databases(), hence registered. Key = attachment id (att_...), index on [uid, env] for export-and-clear.

cookies.$comment: Derived `<short>_*`. The two WIDGET cookies carry no credential and no cookie authenticates the widget API. The two DASHBOARD cookies are a different surface (first-party, server's own origin, owner audience) and are the session + CSRF pair the design specifies; they are listed separately so the widget-side rule stays a rule.

artifacts.$comment: Built widget chunks. Filename derived: `<short>[.<suffix>].js`. Preact lives only in `panels`; the runtime core is vanilla.

identifiers.$comment: Wire-form entity id prefixes. NOT brand-derived: they are entity abbreviations, and they survive a rename untouched.

credentialPrefixes.$comment: Credential literals, DERIVED from brand.short unlike the entity prefixes above. The shape deliberately breaks the three-letter row form: the literal is what gets registered with GitHub secret scanning, so a token pasted into a public repo is reported automatically. A credential must be recognisable as a credential. The spec awards `cdmcp_`, which predates the rename; it is derived here so it cannot drift from the brand again.

metaNames.$comment: Host-authored `<meta name>` keys the widget READS and never mints. Derived `<pkg>:*`, the same namespace as domEvents, which is why an unregistered one looked like an invented DOM event to the linter.: `route` is the ONLY host-authored meta key any spec reads; the build-metadata keys are the and arrive through CaptureContext.build, not the head.

httpHeaders.$comment: The request/response header NAMES inside the `x-<pkg>-` prefix. Registers the PREFIX and scopes it to our own API, and says the individual names are the; they are enumerated HERE because the lint matches the prefix and would otherwise report every one of them as an invented token. Derived `x-<pkg>-*`, so a rename carries them.

domEvents.$comment: CustomEvents on document, mirroring the on() event map. Derived `<pkg>:*`.

symbols.$comment: Symbol.for('<pkg>.*') for patch bookkeeping. The source-level CONSTANTS holding these are named SYM_* so they do not match the env-var grep. `instance` is the BRAND: it is what tells a second copy of the stub that the global it found is ours rather than a host's, which is the difference between first-wins and installing at the collision fallback.

reservedCustom.$comment: Reserved prefix inside CaptureContext.custom. DELIBERATELY NAME-INDEPENDENT and NOT derived: a fixed internal token so the host-facing custom-key contract survives any future rebrand untouched. Registered as the one intentional exception; not rename residue.

budgets.$comment: Keys match `artifacts.suffixes`. gzip:true, brotli:false (a silent switch to brotli relaxes every budget ~15%). RATIFIED 2026-08-12: The spike's bottom-up re-derivation is done, so these are HARD gates now rather than targets — `size-limit` exits 1 on breach, verified by breaching it. The envelope is 40000 BYTES (not 40960), gzip level 9, measured per artefact and summed; each of those three was an ambiguity big enough to decide the question on its own, so `tools/envelope.mjs` asserts them rather than inheriting them. `built` gates the generated .size-limit.json to chunks that currently exist; flip to true as each lands. activationEnvelopeKb 44 = runtime + panels (40 at ratification; raised publicly 2026-08-26) — the row names those two files and gives the stub its OWN 8 KB row, so summing three charged the stub twice. `envelope:false` marks an eager artefact as budgeted separately; `enforced:false` marks a budget as REPORTED rather than gated, which is what the two `— of which` sub-rows are: a decomposition of the 40 with an empty Enforced-by cell; the generator emits the envelope row plus a total row at the sum of every eager budget, so correcting the first leaves no byte unwatched.

stub.$comment: Always loaded, and budgets it on its own row — NOT inside the runtime envelope. envelope:false is what keeps it out of that sum; it is still counted in the total-activation row.

runtime.$comment: Part of the runtime envelope, which is the gate. This per-file number is the own estimate of how the 40 KB would divide and is REPORTED, not enforced — the product divided it 19.5/20.4. Raised 20 -> 20.5 at 0.1.34, which moves the total-activation row (the sum of the eager budgets) from 48 to 48.5 KB: the cached list now follows confirmed edits (+52 B) and every chunk URL carries the real build id instead of 0.0.0 (+13 B), and the total sat 21 B under 48 KB before either. The runtime envelope stays at 44 KB.

panels.$comment: Part of the runtime envelope, which is the gate. This per-file number is the own estimate of how the 40 KB would divide and is REPORTED, not enforced — the product divided it 19.5/20.4. Raised 20 -> 20.5 at 0.1.34, which moves the total-activation row (the sum of the eager budgets) from 48 to 48.5 KB: the cached list now follows confirmed edits (+52 B) and every chunk URL carries the real build id instead of 0.0.0 (+13 B), and the total sat 21 B under 48 KB before either. The runtime envelope stays at 44 KB.

capture.$comment: Built from v0, ahead .1's v0.1 tag. Always specified this home for the redaction module; PLAN inverted it only because isSensitiveValue was believed to be needed at pin time in the eager chunk. It is not: anchor CREATION only happens with the composer open, so capture is lazy like the spec said. lazy:true keeps it out of the activation envelope, which is what the design makes normative. Budget raised 8 -> 12 KB when selector generation landed, and 12 -> 14 when the anchor RECORDER moved in beside it: chooses @medv/finder (~2 KB min+gz) and allocates it inside the anchor core, but GENERATION only happens at creation while RESOLUTION runs on every load — so it belongs in this lazy chunk rather than the eager one. lazy:true keeps it outside the normative activation envelope, which is the sum that is actually gated. Raised 14 -> 15 at the Phase-1 close-out: 01 SS10.3's keyboard virtual cursor lands here, beside the add chrome it draws through, because `add` is unreachable without this chunk. Lazy bytes, so the envelope is untouched — the same trade priced for the dock.

anchorExt.$comment: Built from v0 even though the design makes the v0 cascade `testid` + `css` only and P8 asserts a v0 session fetches NEITHER anchor chunk. Building it is not the same as loading it: the steps shipped inside snag.runtime.js until selector generation landed, and keeping them compiled and tested here is what makes the v0.1 wiring a fetch rather than a rewrite. lazy:true keeps it out of the normative envelope.

anchorFuzzy.$comment: 3 -> 5 at. Draft 4's 3 KB priced 'matchQuote and approx-string-match, the chunk's entire contents' — before the decision made chunks self-contained. The chunk now carries its own TextIndex copy (the collapse machine + build, ~0.9 KB, one SOURCE file shared with snag.text.js) and the pass-budget engine; the scorers are INJECTED from anchor-ext (which is loaded by construction before fuzzy ever escalates) rather than bundled, which is what keeps this at 5 and not 6.5. Lazy, fetched only after the resident and extended steps BOTH missed on a record with a searchable quote — a session with no orphaned text pins never downloads it.

dock.$comment: The funded lever, taken at. The dock opens on demand, so its bytes left the activation envelope. SELF-CONTAINED — it bundles its own Preact copy (16.2 KB gz measured standalone, exactly the prediction), because cross-chunk imports died of module-map poisoning; lazy bytes cost the envelope nothing, which is the whole argument. Raised 21 -> 22 at 0.1.15: the reply box asks who is writing as the composer does, so the sign-in popup and the identity reader ride along here too. Raised 22 -> 23 at 0.1.21: the list header carries the round as its title, always-visible status chips with counts, and sort/filter on one row.

text.$comment: The TENTH artefact: creation-side text picking — the selection watcher, the TextIndex build, quote policy and createTextAnchor. Loaded on entering the text sub-mode of `add`, never before. It exists because the machinery outgrew every existing home: capture's 14 KB is metadata+redaction+recorder and went 2 KB over with this inside; anchor-ext's 4 KB is resolution steps with ~1 KB of headroom. Self-contained — it bundles its own copies of the shared sources (index, labels, selectors), and the resolution-side index copy in anchor-ext is the same one SOURCE file.
